newsitem.title: USA: Chiron herpes results to delay CMV vaccine.
newsitem.headline: Chiron herpes results to delay CMV vaccine.

text.p: Chiron Corp's findings that its genital herpes vaccine candidate is not an effective treatment will also delay the trials of another vaccine to treat CMV, the herpes-like virus that often afflicts AIDS patients, a company spokesman said Monday.
He said the Phase 3 trials of the CMV vaccine would be delayed until at least mid-year 1997. Originally, Chiron had hoped to start those trials by the end of this year.
"We are waiting to finish our analysis of the data (on the herpes virus)," spokesman Larry Kurtz said. "It is a relative of the CMV virus and we think the trial results are relevant."
Kurtz also said that depending on the results of its analysis of the herpes trial, it might decide to not pursue further testing of the CMV virus.
"There is no reason at this point to believe we will or will not conduct further trials (of the CMV vaccine)," Kurtz said. "We need to wait until we finish our analysis."

He said Chiron was interested in examining the herpes trial results more closely since that vaccine did produce strong immune response, which typcially correlates with efficacy. "Since we achieved our goal of high immune response, we are puzzled as to why it was not effective," he said.

Earlier trials of the CMV vaccine also showed a clear immune response. But after the herpes results, Chiron is concerned that immune response will not translate into an effective means of preventing the CMV virus.

CMV, or cytomegalovirus, afflicts people with immune suppression such as those with AIDS or organ transplant recipients. It can lead to blindness, or birth defects in children of those with the virus. -Andrea Orr 213 380-2014
